How to read this: every county below carries a share of the statewide gap, stated in net margin so the levers compare: a recovered Democrat is worth 1, a persuaded voter is worth 2. 2018 is a starting point, not the target — 2018 itself lost by 297,748. What it gives us is proof: 257,391 of these votes were turned out in a real Indiana midterm, so they are recoverable rather than hypothetical. That is the most credible tranche of the gap. A real gap remains beyond it. Priority precincts no one owns yet, biggest asks first. When the geocoded donor export is loaded, each row will also show small-dollar donors nearby — the recruit list. Spine: VEST 2024 precincts (5,146, 92 counties); 2022 joined on state precinct ID at 99.7%; 2018 areally interpolated across the 2021 redraw (88.7% of precincts draw from a single unsplit source — the rest are flagged). 2018 is a floor with evidence behind it, not a winning number: every recovery vote below is one this precinct actually turned out in a real Indiana midterm. Recovering all of it still leaves a gap. Ownership, chair status, donor counts and candidate visits contain NO mock data: they are empty until filled from the commitments sheet, party records, a geocoded donor export, and the scheduler. Turfs and call lists are cut in VAN — the packet references them, it never replaces them. Tier 3/4 precincts get no packet rather than a dismissive one.
